note: Table pairs joined by MORE THAN ONE foreign key. PostgREST cannot guess which FK an embed means: it refuses the whole request with HTTP 300 / PGRST201 and the screen renders nothing. Every embed across a pair listed here must name its constraint — customers!orders_customer_id_fkey ( … ).
why_declared_and_not_derived: 🔴 THE FK TOPOLOGY IS IN NEITHER SOURCE A STATIC CHECK CAN READ. `orders.customer_id`'s foreign key is NOT in the migration corpus — the only mention in supabase/migrations is a COMMENTED-OUT line in 20260916b — because orders/customers predate version control (tech-debt #39, 'live schema not in version control'). And scripts/sql-harness/fixtures/live-schema-public.sql carries columns but no REFERENCES clauses (tech-debt #357, the harness schema is more forgiving than live). A first version of this cap derived pairs from the corpus alone and was GREEN ON THE LIVE DEFECT — it could not have failed, which is [[R-33]]. So the pairs are DECLARED, with the live measurement that produced them, and the corpus is still parsed and UNIONED in so a future double-FK written as a migration is caught with no edit here.
measured: 2026-09-22, live catalog (pg_constraint joined to pg_class, contype='f', grouped by child+parent HAVING count(*) > 1). Re-measure with that query when adding a foreign key.

pairs.became_ambiguous: 20260921b_capture_relink.sql (2026-09-22) — added orders.relinked_from_customer_id REFERENCES customers(id). Six embed sites broke at once, none of them edited; /orders/:id rendered nothing.

THE SAME DOUBLE FK, READ FROM THE OTHER END — 20260921b. PostgREST ambiguity is SYMMETRIC: a customers-based embed of orders also returns HTTP 300 (PGRST201, cardinality one-to-many), PROVEN LIVE 2026-09-22. Nothing embeds this direction today (CustomerDetail reads orders as a SEPARATE query), so this entry guards a hole rather than recording a break — which is the point of declaring it before someone writes it.
